body:
### Problem

`nvim_del_autocmd(id)` errors with `Failed to delete autocmd` when the autocmd ID has already died together with its buffer (buffer-local autocmd deleted via `nvim_buf_delete`). There is no way to distinguish this from a real failure, and caller-side code that tracks autocmd IDs (e.g. `vim.diagnostic`'s once-BufRead autocmd bookkeeping) hits a hard error on a normal sequence of events.

This is exactly the situation in `vim.diagnostic`'s `cleanup_show_autocmd` (`lua/vim/diagnostic/_handlers.lua:133-139`): `show()` on an unloaded buffer registers a buffer-local once-BufRead autocmd and stores its ID in `ns.user_data[autocmd_key]`; `cleanup_show_autocmd` later deletes the stored ID unconditionally whenever it is non-nil. If the buffer was deleted in between (e.g. by a buffer-cleanup plugin / user), the ID is already dead and the next `show()` on the same namespace throws `Failed to delete autocmd` at the user.

Related: #42094 touches the same show-on-unloaded-buffer path.

### Steps to reproduce

```lua
local aug = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup('r2', { clear = true })
local buf = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(false, true)
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('BufRead', { buf = buf, once = true, callback = function() end, group = aug })
local id = vim.api.nvim_get_autocmds({ group = 'r2' })[1].id
vim.api.nvim_buf_delete(buf, {})                 -- autocmd dies with the buffer
print(#vim.api.nvim_get_autocmds({ group = 'r2' }))  -- 0: already gone
vim.api.nvim_del_autocmd(id)                     -- hard error
```

### Expected behavior

Deleting an already-dead autocmd ID should be a no-op (or at least distinguishable from other failures), so cleanup paths like `vim.diagnostic`'s don't error on IDs that died with their buffer.

### Actual behavior

`E5108: Error executing lua: Failed to delete autocmd` (via pcall: `false, "Failed to delete autocmd"`).

### Neovim version

NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1464+g57d97e513d
title: api: nvim_del_autocmd errors on autocmd ID that died with its buffer (breaks vim.diagnostic show-on-unloaded cleanup)
